As the primary assembler of the iPhone, contract manufacturer Foxconn has long derived more than half of its revenue from the Cupertino-based company.

However, according to the most recent quarter's data, that proportion has fallen below 29%, and the company says this shift will be permanent, causing concern among investors...

Foxconn's Zhengzhou factory is massive, and the city where it is located is colloquially known in China as "iPhone City." At its peak, roughly 80% of the world's iPhone production took place at this single facility.

Although Apple has been working to diversify iPhone production beyond China, Foxconn has remained the company's primary assembly partner. However, in the most recent quarter, the proportion of revenue from this business has dropped below 29%.

The reason is not related to a decrease in the number of iPhones the company produces, but rather to the number of AI servers it is currently manufacturing, according to a report by TNW.

The company says this shift will be permanent.

Fellow Apple supplier TSMC is also experiencing rapid growth in the AI sector.

However, given the talk of an AI bubble in the market, investors are wary of this trend. Although Foxconn's stock price has risen 17% this year, it still lags far behind the 57% gain of Taiwanese companies overall.
